newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid prices steady to down with crude.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid prices steady to down with crude.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices were unchanged to slightly lower Monday in sluggish trade, weighed down by the recent slide in crude and relatively bearish weather forecasts, industry sources said.
"Utilities aren't burning much, and if we're waiting for (hot) weather, it doesn't look like we're getting much anytime soon," said one cash trader.

Despite forecasts for a minor, midweek heat wave in the Northeast, the warmer weather was expected to be short-lived, and the East and Gulf Coast were forecast to range mostly from normal to slightly-below normal right into next week.

In New York Harbor, physical one percent held relatively steady at $16.00-25 a barrel though some still pegged the best buyers in the high-$15s. Traders said July one percent paper sold early at $15.95, off 15 cents with crude, then recovered to the low-$16s.
While supply and demand were fairly well-balanced, traders said the lack of hot weather could soon tilt the scales in favor of the bears.
"The key going forward is if it gets hot enough to generate some burn. Without (hot) weather, buying requirements will be pushed back," said another trader.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour notionally slipped slightly to about $16.50 in the face of no real utility demand.
High sulphurs in New York also lost some ground, with 2.2 percent now talked on either side of $15, traders said.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent was stable at $16.00-25, while three percent was 15 cents lower at about $14.50.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.

The prospects this week for hotter Northeast weather firmed New York city gate gas prices Monday by more than five cents to the mid-to-high $2.40s/mmBtu, or $15.56 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, again stayed little changed at about $2.18/mmBtu, or $13.73 a barrel.
